title: Trump Is Facing a Very Different North Korea
gist: Teaser (paywalled after intro) by Stephen E. Biegun and Emma Chanlett-Avery: Trump wants to restart diplomacy with Kim Jong Un (and scaled back drills with South Korea on Aug. 17), but faces a very different North Korea and needs a new strategy.

themes.theme: Trump's push to restart Kim diplomacy

insights.claim: In an August 17 Truth Social post, Donald Trump announced the US would scale back joint military drills with South Korea, citing his 'very good relationship with Kim Jong Un'.
insights.speaker: Stephen E. Biegun
insights.so_what: Unilateral US concessions on alliance drills may unsettle Seoul and Tokyo; watch Korean peninsula risk and alliance cohesion.
insights.quote: “based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un,”

insights.claim: Trump has suggested in recent media comments that he is in communication with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and has not been subtle about wanting to restart diplomacy, with an eye on his legacy.
insights.speaker: Stephen E. Biegun
insights.so_what: A Trump-Kim summit is a live possibility; headlines could move Korean assets.
insights.quote: Trump has not been subtle about his desire to restart diplomacy with Kim

insights.claim: Stephen E. Biegun and Emma Chanlett-Avery argue that Trump now faces a very different North Korea than in his first term, so his previous approach will not work and he needs a new strategy.
insights.speaker: Stephen E. Biegun
insights.so_what: Expect any new Trump-Kim diplomacy to yield less than hoped; denuclearization unlikely to be on the table on old terms.
insights.quote: And Now He Needs a New Strategy
